interpretations: profile.named_pipe_as_file and tui.named_pipe_as_file treat a Windows named pipe as the FIFO analog of K14 (K14 names a FIFO, socket, device or directory); the contract does not name Windows pipes. Escalated.

agent.regular_file_not_modified is an X1 task criterion: section 3 says the Windows --socket path is a named pipe, and section 1 forbids writes only outside paths named on the command line, so the contract does not literally forbid writing to a named regular file.
tui.ctrl_c_event (a CTRL_C_EVENT raised by another process) is recorded, not gated: tests/g02 gates the Ctrl-C key only (tui.ctrl_c), not an explicit SIGINT to the TUI.

limitations: One host: the owner's Windows 11 Pro 26300 x64 PC, non-elevated user. Three full runs (Windows PowerShell 5.1 twice, PowerShell 7.6.6 once) gave identical verdicts for every row; timing values differ between runs.

Console coverage is pseudoconsole only (CreatePseudoConsole driven by P/Invoke, judged on a small VT screen model; harness.screen_model_unit covers the model). A classic conhost window, Windows Terminal and the legacy console were not exercised; no window was created on the owner's desktop.

Console Ctrl-C was delivered two ways: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent from a separate process attached to the console (Send-ConsoleCtrl.ps1; harness.ctrlc_control_direct proves delivery to a plain child) and ^C typed into the console input. CTRL_BREAK is recorded only. CTRL_CLOSE/LOGOFF/SHUTDOWN events were not tested.

Timing: process exit times are the kernel exit time (GetProcessTimes) compared with the sender's timestamp taken just before GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent (same clock); TUI waits poll the screen every ~3 ms.

Not covered: a second Windows account (pipe DACL from another user), remote (SMB) pipe clients, interop with the real Win32-OpenSSH ssh-agent (the owner's agent must not be contacted; the fixture agent stands in), ARM64 Windows, paths longer than MAX_PATH, UNC working directories, console code pages other than the default, SmartScreen/Mark-of-the-Web (files were copied through WSL and carry no Zone.Identifier), Defender behaviour, launching the .exe from WSL through interop.

The artifacts ran with PATH reduced to %SystemRoot%\System32 and its WindowsPowerShell directory (%SystemRoot% itself is left out because the Python launcher py.exe lives there on this host); env.no_toolchain_on_path found no Go, Rust, C, Node, Bun, Deno, Python, zig or git.
Resolution-order, .cmd and lone-surrogate rows are recorded observations (info or non-gating), not contract verdicts.
The X1 Windows script is new in this task; its controls passed, but it has had no independent review yet.
